#144673 769 2006-02-16T22:31:26Z Teh Dude
Bear in mind that the sequence in which the numbers appear does not matter.

For those of you who are a little dense, let me explain why this is. You get a new number every time you load the page. This implies that the numbers are being generated by a script. The script generates a new number based either on the last number or on the time or at random (either totally random or picked randomly from a list). Now all of these options, except for the first one, would produce numbers that are not in any order. The first option produces numbers in order but there are loads of people loading up NUMA each second.

So if I have my magic sequence 1 1 2 3 5 8 13 21. Say kai loads NUMA first. He gets 1. But then kirby loads it and takes the next 1. Wedgie comes along and gets 2. Now when kai loads the site he gets 3. He comes back later and gets 13.

So kai has 1,3,13 and he thinks "wtf is this pile of <expletive deleted>".

The only way you could get the numbers in sequence is with cookies so the script knows how far you are with the sequence and can give you a new number based on this. I tried deleting all numa cookies then revisiting the front page. No cookies were created.

A further fault with giving numbers in sequence is that even if kai was given 1 1 2 3 5 8 13 21, what would happen if he forgot one of the numbers or if he pressed reload twice by accident?

I hope that this explains why the sequence in which the numbers appear does not matter.

Quote: Minitrue
This message has been deemed doubleplusungood crimethink by Minitrue.  You know, thirty years ago we didn't have crimethink at all.  Things were simpler.  A Ministry knew his place in the world.  Of course, this was all before the War.  I was in the war.  Did I ever tell you that?  Private Minitrue.  Heh heh.  That brings back memories.  I remember when we first touched foot on enemy soil.  We saw the jungle just a few clicks ahead and the sergeant called for us all to partner up and search for enemies.  'Course I went with Leo.
Leo and I were like brothers. He was nearly bald.  He had an effeminate look about him.  He was narrow and tall, standing about six and a half feet.  He didn't have proper diction but that didn't matter.  He was rather intuitive and I felt safe with him.
When we ventured out into the darkness of the jungle, everything became dead silent.  Leo looked over at me and nodded.  He was taking the lead.  I readied my rifle and followed closely behind.  The air was thick soup.  Rain began to fall; it picked up quickly and became a raging tempest around us.  Despite the storm, the world was quiet.  The rain filled the world with a solid noise, like that of loud fan.  Nothing in the jungle moved.  It was a single frame of reality drawn out into hours.  We ventured for nearly half a day in a humming, motionless world.  It was beyond surreal.  It was like nothing I had ever seen.  There was a matte-like glow to the jungle, as if it were filled with fluourescent lights.  My world seemed fake.
After a time, Leo reclined against a rock and said we ought to rest.  I didn't feel tired.  I laid myself on the jungle bed.  It was hard like concrete.  My mind started wandering.  Would I ever make it back home?  Would I ever be able to see my kids again?  What would become of Miniluv in my absense?  I bunched some moss beneath me.  I laid my head upon the moss and began to slumber.  The sleep was fitful and felt eternal.  It was dreamless.  I could swear I was somehow conscious the whole time.
I awoke after an immeasurable length of time to gunfire in the north.  Leo was already awake.  He was chattering on the radio with the sarge.
"We gotta go, Mini," Leo shouted.
"Let's do this," I replied.

#144777 801 2006-02-17T02:50:02Z AlliedEnvy
Quote: Kablizzy, Feb 14 2006, 04:34 AM
Quote
The sun aligns with the fallen;

Hundreds exist, yet within each, Four meet as one.

Below, the watcher protects;

While the blue vein brings life to them all.

Millions golden, sun-glinted and windswept.

Now, you may think you know the answer to this, but there is more than one answer (Particularly directed at Trogdor).

Okay. The poem. Everyone has pretty much ignored the poem so far, or thrown out random guesses that don't connect to anything.

First of all, Kablizzy uses a QUOTE around the poem. Whether he uses it to separate the text or if he's actually quoting from something, we don't know. I'd be interested to see if we could find a source for this poem, or if it's something Kablizzy made up.

One thing we do know is that Trogdor knows something about this poem. He seems to either not know what Kablizzy thinks he knows, or he just isn't saying. Perhaps we should look back at what he says on this.

We also know that there is more than one answer to the poem. Which strikes me as odd, because there is no question in it. It's just description. Perhaps he means there is more than one interpretation, but maybe that is a conclusion that should not be jumped to. I don't really know where to go on this, or if it's a non-clue.

Okay, so the poem itself. I'll go line-by-line.

"The sun aligns with the fallen;"

The fallen what? Is this a reference to something in the metanet community, or something outside?
Are these things that have literally 'fallen', or things that have figuratively 'fallen'?

There are a heck of a lot of definitions for fallen. Which one(s) is Kablizzy using?

Is the sun what it seems to be? Maybe it's a play on 'son'. Maybe it really refers to something else. Hrm.

'Aligns'. What are we talking about here? A geometrical alignment? A philosophical alignment? Some other sort of alignment?

"Hundreds exist, yet within each, Four meet as one."

Hundreds of what? There are lots of sets of hundreds of things. This is really vague.

'Four'. Kablizzy capitalizes this in the middle of the sentence. This means that it is important in some way. In fact, I think just about everything Kablizzy has capitalised in the middle of a sentence will be somehow important in solving this. Maybe Four really refers to something else. I'm thinking maybe COFFEE here, but that's just a wild guess.

'within each' i.e. each of the hundreds, right?

'Four meet as one.' This is quite odd. Again, this sounds like COFFEE, but I'm not certain. Four what? Something tangible or not? And the one, same thing, is it tangible or not? What is this referring to?

"Below, the watcher protects;"

This is also odd - usually a watcher watches from above. Maybe it's not one who watches, but in fact, someone who uses a watch in some fashion? Doesn't really seem to fit.

'the watcher protects'. What are they protecting? How? For what reason? Why are they below? This is also very vague.

"While the blue vein brings life to them all."

Presumedly this means that this line is happening while the watcher protects.

'blue vein'. What is this referring to? There are multiple definitions for vein. Which are we talking about here?

The 'blue vein brings life to them all'. Them all being the hundreds? How does it bring life? Are we talking literally, or figuratively?

"Millions golden, sun-glinted and windswept."

This is worded somewhat weirdly. I would have switched windswept and sun-glinted. Better rhythm.

'Millions' of what? Same as the 'hundreds', or different?

'golden, sun-glinted and windswept.' What things are golden, sun-glinted, and windswept? Hair? Plants of some sort? Sand grains? Something else? There are millions of them, whatever they are.


This is all very terribly vague to me. Maybe it ties into some of the other clues we have uncovered. Whatever it is, I believe it's important in some way.

Okay, now here's a crazy thought struck after much fruitless googling-
What if I'm looking for meaning where there is none? What if there's some previously unseen message in all this?

For the eighth is always on the hour,
the twenty being on the min-ute
The one is left trailing far behind,

finute, as in finite. Doubtfull, but it trumps the rest of my research on nigerian money scammers.

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_August

Actually, now I'm leaning towards this being simpler- if, indeed, the second stanza is simple enough to incorporate a simple time- to 8:21
"The twenty being on the min"
Except that, 1 is not exactly trailing FAR behind...

Some more, collected thoughts
Okay, with some different punctuation, the first verse can make a bit more sense...

A heart is a precious thing to waste,
It beats- but once a year,
When cupid pulls his arrow string,
Its target is always clear.

So. The hearts target is clear but once a year, when cupid pulls his arrow string. That day seems to me to be most likey Valentines Day, which seems appropriate seeing how recent it was.

For the eighth is always on the hour,
the twenty being on the min.
The one is left trailing far behind,
And that is where we fin.

Okay. Now. This is still very unclear to me, but something worth consider is that we have the whole 'always' thing returning for this verse;
Its target is "always" clear, and the eighth is "always" on the hour. So. There's a chance this thing is talking about this occuring always at the time specified, or maybe it's something like a clock out of batteries, stuck on this time. I don't know, but I think (and hope) that it's the former.
Which leaves with a time on Valentines day: Either 8:21 or 8:20 and 1 second... I'd say 8:21. And, when this point is 'always' reached, the heart... looses it's purpose? And this is where we fin... could this be talking about death?

I mean, this is all pure speculation in the hope that it'll spark something in a mind better than my own, but they're some thoughts, and they do seem to tie in- slightly- with

They say a sucker is born every minute. I fully believe this to be true.

Okay. So. Rather than a birth, as I was thinking before, could be somebody who died- or what they died of- at 8:21 on Valentines Day.
There's some rather hefty leaps from the poem to that conclusion, but once again, it beats the rest of my theories...

Anyway, I've been doing some analysis of Kablizzys final clue, in the hope he hasn't just typed it like that to force us to try to find meaning where there is none... and so, I present to you, the letters- in order of colour, as seen through the refraction of light. (ROY. G. BIV, anybody?) Darker letters come after lighter ones.

So...
u,u,h

RED:c,v,s
ORANGE: o,o
y,y
(None for Green)
eta[color=DARKBLUE]h
n
ie

Where this gets us, I'm not quite sure, but I've had further thoughts-
Some of the fonts- Impact, Optima and Geneva (for instance), begin with letters of ROYGBIV, which represents the spectrum of the rainbow... maybe letters there could be slotted into the appropriate slot. And the tags for bold and italic start with B and I- for Blue and Indigo, respetively.

What we'd do with the other fonts and underlines, I'm not sure.

But still, I'll arrange it like this, just because I can: (Note that all 'gray' letters are now under G, for Gray, and letters that double up aren't posted here...)
OTHER: ALVEIN
R: OCSV
O: OTG
Y: Y
G: NYEUH
B: ETHA
I: NDREL
V: EI

I'm very sorry if I missed anything and for the lack of doubling up, but that's my attempt to catagorise every letter in the thing under catagories of the colours of the rainbow...

Roy. G. Biv's a jerk.
Okay, so using the list I was fiddling with a while ago, I decided to try adding the number of different letters under each 'catagory' to the letter that catagory began with, to come up with a different series of letters...

R+4= V
O+3= R
Y+1= Z
G+5= L
B+4= F
I+5= N
V+2= X

(Other+6=x+6)

Okay, so, that's definately pure nonsense- it doesn't even have any vowels...
But, what IF the letters under 'other' are added to 'O' (for Orange), then you'd get...

R+4= V
O+9= X
Y+1= Z
G+5= L
B+4= F
I+5= N
V+2= X

Still not good. Maybe the amounts of letters under the catagories should have counted for ALL of the letters in the passage...

But a prelimary scan of the sorts of letters you'd probably end up with seems to make that seem highly unlikely. So, I *think* this means that the ROYGBIV approach isn't going to get us anywhere. Relating to Sweeps stuff

Oh, goodness!

I just had a thought, laying on my bed and looking on my bookshelf...

The Carlyle group- as referenced by Sweep on the madness temple hosted Legacy thingy (Seen here: http://www.madnesstemple.com/legacy/) is none other but that thingy that Michael Moore was talking about for part of Fahrenheit 9/11. I can vagualy remember that, and it was something to do with Bin Ladens family, I think...

A quick google search showed that this was true, coming up with many bin laden/ bush/ carlyle group references, and also THIS:
Quote: http://www.carlyle.com/eng/geo/casestudy-2226.html
Carlyle Realty Partners has successfully exited 74 Grand Street, a 300,000 square foot redeveloped office building in Jersey City, New Jersey.

In June 1999, Carlyle entered into the redevelopment of 74 Grand to take advantage of increasingly tight leasing conditions in Manhattan.  Carlyle and its partner, SJP Properties, delivered the building for a cost of $145 per square foot, which represents a 50 percent discount to Manhattan building values and 30 percent below Jersey City values.  "With this advantage, we were able to seize on demand from financial services companies that were seeking lower-cost space outside Manhattan," says Gabe Finke, Carlyle's Principal who led the deal.

Carlyle completed a full-building lease with Merrill Lynch at rents 16 percent above original budget and well ahead of the projected lease-up pace.  After completing the lease, Carlyle sold the building in March 2001.  Over a 21-month hold period, the investment generated a 2.5x equity multiple and approximately $17 million of profit.

George Bush's father works for the Carlyle group, and the carlyle group made much money from the War on Terrorism (You know the war, right? The one where they liberated oil?)

There's a whole lot of information in Fahrenheit 9/11 (Of which I have the book, which I'm planning on rereading to refresh my knowledge and maybe get a better idea of how this may tie in with this), but there's also plenty of websites around... a skim read of this one: http://www.truthout.org/docs_01/01.11F.Arms.Carlyle.p.htm - seems to be looking very helpfull, too, for anybody else interested.

The problem is, I don't know how this relates to Kablizzy's clue, though Sweep has told me that his clues are unrelated to Kablizzy's- though they should lead to the same conclusion/ word, the two do not tie in together- people can work them out using only one set.

So. I'm considering working on this, and doing some research (Though, right now, I really should be studying...) on The Carlyle Group and their move to New Jersey...

But Wait- There's SO MUCH MORE just 'discovered' by me...

Allright. Adding in 'anon' to the google search of keywords from Sweeps legacy thing, guess what? I found a sight that has the same message, pretty much word for word, as what Sweep has hosted on the legacy thing. Furthermore, what's the site called? Radiohead News. Guess who sweep's favourite band is? Radiohead.

Here's the website: http://www.ateaseweb.com/news/
Here's the relevant post: Radiohead is dead, long live The Carlyle Group

Two new posts again on Dead Air Space tonight.

nr. 1:

If you cant beat em, join em.

We have decided to change the name of the band to

THE CARLYLE GROUP

for tax reasons and are moving our offices to Jersey.

Thank you. That'll be all.

Anon

nr 2:

i was looking for a drum machine and found this.

http://www.albinoblacksheep.com/flash/drum.php

Thom

[Posted by adriaan at 01:24 AM, February 17, 2006]

Okay...
So. I figure it's some Radiohead themed political swipe at the carlyle group by the alternative band... Written by Radiohead, perhaps?

Anyway, the ONLY inconsistancy between the two messages- the one on Sweeps website, ande the one on the Radiohead News website, is the word band, instead of Project.

I'm still poised to do some more research on the Carlyle group if this turns out not to be the answer, but I'm currently putting my money on the word band.

I'm just going to check to see if there's any obvious way you could get the same answer from Kablizzy's clue, but I'm fairly confident that's the last word.
